chapter: New Orleans bands, Louis and the Lyric
title: Seeing Count Basie and Lovie Taylor's dancing in St. Louis shows
summary: In St. Louis they saw Count Basie with Gonzelle White on the burlesque wheel, plus Rose Marie and Chu Chin Chow. Jasper Taylor's drumming in Joe Jordan's band backed the soft-shoe dancer Lovie Taylor.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: You know what, when we first saw Count Basie. He was playing for Gonzelle White.
You saw him then?
Yes. On the Columbia Burlesque Wheel.
That's right.
Where was that?
In St. Louis.
Oh, I see.
Because I cared less about the theater and I told Zutty you have to sit up in the balcony.
We saw Rose Marie. We saw, what was it some other big show we saw?
So many shows.
'Chin Chow....'
Yes, 'Chin Chow Chin.'
What was that called? Yes, I remember that. I saw that. 'Chou Chin Chow?'
Yes, that's what he wanted to do.
We saw more than that. This other fine show on the Burlesque Wheel with Jasper Taylor was playing drums. Jasper Taylor was in Joe

Jordan's band. And they played 'Sweet Georgia Brown' for a cat to dance by the name of Lovie Taylor. Boy and did that cat dance. And that music was so perfect behind this cat's taps. He was a tap dancer but it was soft shoe. He didn't have no taps on his shoes.
It's a more subtle thing really than straight tap.
Yes, oh boy and that music. And that cat was dancing right with that music. Do you remember that Marge?
Yes.
The music had to be soft.
Oh, very soft.
Well that's what we would do on our nights off.
And they were playing the melody so beautifully.
